payload.task_text:
The product team wants to analyze customer review quality across product categories to prioritize product improvement efforts. Query WooCommerce product review data and link it to product categories to understand how different categories perform with customers.

Create an Excel file called Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx with two sheets. The first sheet should be called "Category Analysis" with columns: Category, Product_Count, Review_Count, Avg_Rating (rounded to 2 decimal places), Five_Star_Count, and Five_Star_Rate (the percentage of reviews that are 5 stars, rounded to 1 decimal). Sort by Category alphabetically. The second sheet should be called "Top Products" and list the top 10 highest-rated products that have at least 3 reviews, with columns: Product_Name (truncated to 50 characters if needed), Category, Review_Count, and Avg_Rating (rounded to 2 decimal places). Sort by Avg_Rating descending, then Review_Count descending.

Create a Notion database called "Product Review Insights" with properties for Category (title), Product_Count (number), Review_Count (number), Avg_Rating (number), and Five_Star_Rate (number). Populate it with one entry per category from the Category Analysis sheet.

Email the analysis to product_team@store.com with subject "Product Review Analysis Report" and include a summary of which categories have the highest and lowest ratings in the email body.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use two genuine dependency waves with exactly three sub-agents total. The first agent computes the complete store join once; the two artifact writers then run in parallel from one canonical category table.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 Explore sub-agent:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Use one Explore sub-agent to retrieve the complete product and review endpoints read-only using `perPage=100` and increasing pages until each has a short or empty terminal page. Omit the optional review `status` argument, preserve every observed status, and filter only as the original task requires. Join strictly by Product_ID; a product contributes to each observed category exactly according to its source categories. Compute the compact per-category Product_Count, Review_Count, rating sum/average, Five_Star_Count/Rate, and the eligible products with at least three reviews. Rank Top Products by average rating descending, review count descending, then stable Product_ID. Return the full compact category and top-ten tables directly, plus endpoint page/row/status controls, join/category coverage, and duplicate/tie checks. Do not modify the store or create deliverables.

After Wave 1, the main agent independently checks the counts, rates, rankings, and tie order, then freezes one immutable category/top-product handoff for both writers.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 3 Coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one Coder sub-agent as the sole writer of `Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx`. Create the exact two sheets once from the frozen tables, with exact headers, truncation, sorting, row limits, rounding, and literal values. Read both sheets back and return the path plus complete row/value controls.

   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one Coder sub-agent as the sole owner of the exact-title `Product Review Insights` database. Search exact title once first and reuse an exact match, otherwise create the database once with the exact property types; then create exactly one page per frozen category, sending each page in a SINGLE create call that carries all its properties together — never update properties one at a time, never re-read pages between inserts, and do not verify row-by-row. When all rows are inserted, issue ONE final database query to confirm the row count, and return the database ID, property names and final row count. Do not write the workbook.

   3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): Use one Coder sub-agent as the sole owner of the summary email to product_team@store.com with the exact task subject: body built ONLY from the frozen tables — the total product/review counts, the highest-rated and lowest-rated categories with their average ratings and five-star rates, and the complete per-category breakdown. Paginate Sent search and match the exact recipient/subject before an at-most-once send, then read the retained message back and return its ID. Do not write the workbook or database.

After all three writers return, reconcile every category across source, workbook, database and the sent message against the same frozen tables. Read back all three outputs. Repairs belong only to the original writer, and there is no separate validation wave.

After the final wave completes, do not invoke the agent-dispatch tool again — not even an empty or exploratory dispatch attempt (a dispatch that returns zero agents is wasted work). Any remaining checks, emails or small writes are main-agent direct work completed in one pass.

nodes.text:
You are a READ-ONLY exploration agent working on a customer review quality analysis for a WooCommerce store. Do NOT create, modify, or delete anything in the store, and do NOT create any files. Your job is to fetch the complete product and review data, join them by Product_ID, and compute two canonical analysis tables that downstream artifacts (Excel, Notion, email) will be built from.

STEP 1 — Fetch ALL products:
- Call mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list with perPage=100, page=1, then page=2, 3, ... until a page returns FEWER than 100 items (or an empty array). Record the number of pages fetched and the total distinct product count.
- For every product keep: id, name, categories (list of {id, name}).

STEP 2 — Fetch ALL reviews:
- Call mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_reviews_list with perPage=100, page=1, then page=2, 3, ... until a short/empty terminal page. IMPORTANT: do NOT pass the `status` argument — fetch every review regardless of status and preserve each review's status field.
- For every review keep: id, product_id, rating, status. Record the count per status (e.g. approved/hold/spam/trash).

STEP 3 — Fetch ALL categories:
- Call mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_categories_list with perPage=100 (paginate if needed) to build the map category_id -> category_name.

STEP 4 — Join & compute:
- Join reviews to products STRICTLY by Product_ID (a review belongs to the product whose id equals review.product_id).
- Per category (every category present in the store, including any with zero reviews): Product_Count = number of DISTINCT products whose categories include that category; Review_Count = number of reviews whose product is in that category; Avg_Rating = mean rating of those reviews (report UNROUNDED, full precision); Five_Star_Count = count of those reviews with rating == 5; Five_Star_Rate = Five_Star_Count / Review_Count * 100 (report UNROUNDED; use 0 when Review_Count == 0).
- Overall totals: total distinct products (across all pages) and total reviews (across all pages).
- Eligible products: products with >= 3 reviews total (all statuses). For each, compute Review_Count and Avg_Rating (full precision). Rank by Avg_Rating DESC, then Review_Count DESC, then Product_ID ASC as the stable tie-break. Take the TOP 10.
- For each top-10 product report: Product_ID, Product_Name (full name, do NOT truncate), the product's category names JOINED with ", " in source order, plus the raw category list so I can verify, Review_Count, and Avg_Rating (full precision).
- Highest-rated category and lowest-rated category by Avg_Rating considering only categories with Review_Count > 0 (if no category has reviews, state that explicitly).

STEP 5 — Return your final report containing EXACTLY these sections:
A. CONTROLS: pages fetched (products), pages fetched (reviews), total distinct product count, total review count, review status distribution (status -> count), category count, duplicate product IDs found (list or none), duplicate review IDs found (list or none), reviews whose product_id has NO matching product (count + ids), products with no categories (count + names).
B. CATEGORY TABLE (complete, one row per category): Category | Product_Count | Review_Count | Avg_Rating (unrounded) | Five_Star_Count | Five_Star_Rate (unrounded).
C. TOP 10 PRODUCTS TABLE: Product_ID | Product_Name | Category (joined ", ") | raw category list | Review_Count | Avg_Rating (unrounded).
D. OVERALL TOTALS: total products, total reviews.
E. HIGHEST/LOWEST: highest-rated category (name, avg rating, review count) and lowest-rated category (name, avg rating, review count) among categories with Review_Count > 0.

Be exhaustive and precise — your output is the single canonical data source for the whole pipeline. Do not omit any category or any of the 10 ranked products.
Explore WooCommerce review data

You are the sole writer of an Excel workbook for a WooCommerce customer review quality analysis. The data has already been computed and verified — do NOT re-query WooCommerce, do NOT recompute anything. Use ONLY the frozen tables below.

1. If the file does not exist yet, create it with mcp__excel__create_workbook (filepath as above).

If the default workbook has a sheet named "Sheet1" (or similar), rename/remove it so only the two required sheets exist; if a sheet with the required name already exists, overwrite its contents rather than creating a duplicate.

RULES:
- Write literal values exactly as specified; do not add extra columns, extra rows, formulas, charts, or formatting unless trivial (bold headers are optional).
- Do NOT create any other files or artifacts, and do NOT touch WooCommerce/Notion/email.

AFTER WRITING, VERIFY: use mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata and mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel to read BOTH sheets back completely. Confirm: exactly 2 sheets with the exact names; sheet 1 has 7 rows (header + 8) = actually 9 rows total (header + 8 data rows) and sheet 2 has 11 rows total (header + 10 data rows); every cell value matches the frozen tables (including truncated product names and the numeric precision).

RETURN: the absolute file path, the exact sheet names, the total row/column counts per sheet, and a full listing of the values read back from both sheets (so the coordinator can reconcile).
Write Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx

You are the sole owner of a Notion database creation task for a WooCommerce customer review quality analysis. The data has already been computed and verified — do NOT re-query WooCommerce, do NOT recompute anything, and do NOT touch Excel or email. Use ONLY the frozen tables below and the mcp__notion__* tools.

STEP 1 — SEARCH FIRST: Call mcp__notion__API-post-search with query "Product Review Insights" (no filter). If there is an EXACT match — an existing database whose title is exactly "Product Review Insights" — REUSE it (use its database_id) and do not create a new one. If no exact match exists, create the database ONCE with mcp__notion__API-create-a-database with title "Product Review Insights" and parent = a page (search for a suitable parent page if needed, e.g. any page returned by a search; if none, use the workspace root). If the create call returns an error about an existing title, search again and reuse the exact match.

STEP 2 — DATABASE SCHEMA (must be exactly these 5 properties, no extra ones):
- Category (type: title)
- Product_Count (type: number)
- Review_Count (type: number)
- Avg_Rating (type: number)
- Five_Star_Rate (type: number)

STEP 3 — INSERT ONE PAGE PER CATEGORY: For EACH of the 8 categories below, create exactly one page in the database with mcp__notion__API-post-page, passing parent = {"database_id": <db id>, "type": "database_id"} and ALL properties together in the SINGLE properties argument of that one create call (title property "Category" as a title array, the rest as number objects). Do NOT create a page and then update properties one at a time; do NOT re-read pages between inserts; do NOT verify row-by-row during insertion.

Frozen category rows (Category, Product_Count, Review_Count, Avg_Rating, Five_Star_Rate):
Audio, 15, 78, 4.47, 62.8
Cameras, 10, 49, 4.69, 73.5
Electronics, 30, 149, 4.57, 68.5
Headphones, 10, 50, 4.52, 64.0
Home Appliances, 8, 29, 4.72, 72.4
Speakers, 5, 28, 4.39, 60.7
TV & Home Theater, 13, 63, 4.78, 77.8
Watches, 6, 28, 4.43, 53.6

Note: Notion property values for number properties should be plain JSON numbers (e.g. {"number": 4.47}); the title property value must be an array of rich text objects with content = category name.

STEP 4 — FINAL VERIFICATION (ONE query only): After all 8 pages are inserted, call mcp__notion__API-post-database-query ONCE on the database (page_size=100) and confirm the row count is 8.

RETURN: the database ID, the exact property names (in order), and the final confirmed row count from the query. Do not create any files.
Create Notion Product Review Insights DB

You are the sole owner of a summary email for a WooCommerce customer review quality analysis. The data has already been computed and verified — do NOT re-query WooCommerce, do NOT recompute anything, and do NOT touch Excel or Notion. Use ONLY the frozen numbers below and the mcp__emails__* tools.

TARGET: send ONE email to product_team@store.com with subject exactly "Product Review Analysis Report".

STEP 1 — CHECK FOR EXISTING SEND (at-most-once): Paginate through the Sent folder (mcp__emails__get_emails folder="Sent", page_size=100, page=1,2,... until a short/empty page; also try mcp__emails__search_emails query="Product Review Analysis Report" if needed). Look for any email whose recipient matches product_team@store.com AND subject is exactly "Product Review Analysis Report". If such an email ALREADY exists, do NOT send again — skip to STEP 4 using that existing email's ID. Otherwise proceed to STEP 2.

STEP 2 — SEND: mcp__emails__send_email with:
- to: "product_team@store.com"
- subject: "Product Review Analysis Report"
- body: plain-text body built ONLY from the frozen facts below (structure it cleanly, e.g. a greeting line, a summary paragraph naming the highest- and lowest-rated categories with their average ratings and five-star rates, the overall totals, and the complete per-category breakdown; optionally a sign-off).

FROZEN FACTS (do not alter any number):
- Total products: 82
- Total reviews: 396

- Lowest-rated category: Speakers — Avg Rating 4.39, Five-Star Rate 60.7%
- Complete per-category breakdown (Category: Product_Count, Review_Count, Avg_Rating, Five_Star_Rate):
  Audio: 15, 78, 4.47, 62.8
  Cameras: 10, 49, 4.69, 73.5
  Electronics: 30, 149, 4.57, 68.5
  Headphones: 10, 50, 4.52, 64.0
  Home Appliances: 8, 29, 4.72, 72.4
  Speakers: 5, 28, 4.39, 60.7
  TV & Home Theater: 13, 63, 4.78, 77.8
  Watches: 6, 28, 4.43, 53.6

STEP 3 — CONFIRM SEND: After sending, paginate the Sent folder again (or search) to find the retained message matching recipient product_team@store.com and subject "Product Review Analysis Report". Read it back with mcp__emails__read_email (or get its headers) to confirm it was sent.

STEP 4 — RETURN: the email ID of the retained message, the exact recipient, the exact subject, and a short excerpt of the body that was sent (or, if an existing email was found in STEP 1, its ID and confirmation it was not duplicated). Do not create any files.
